faqs.question: How do you say happy Raksha Bandhan in Bengali?
faqs.answer: শুভ রাখী পূর্ণিমা (shubho Rakhi Purnima) is the natural greeting, and শুভ রাখী বন্ধন (shubho Rakhi Bandhan) also works. A transliterated "Happy Raksha Bandhan" is understood everywhere but reads as imported rather than Bengali.

faqs.question: Is Raksha Bandhan called something different in Bengal?
faqs.answer: Yes. In Bengali the day is usually রাখী পূর্ণিমা (Rakhi Purnima) or simply রাখী, and "Raksha Bandhan" is the pan-Indian name. Every Bengali-language page ranking for this query uses রাখী পূর্ণিমা in the body while keeping "Raksha Bandhan" in the headline.

faqs.question: Should I write তুমি or তুই to my elder brother?
faqs.answer: তুমি. The peer-reviewed study of Bengali person deixis in the International Journal of English Linguistics classes তুই as the intimate/impolite/neglecting form and records that it is what elders in a family use downward, to address younger members. Sent upward to a দাদা it inverts the direction the pronoun normally travels.

faqs.question: When should I use আপনি in a rakhi message?
faqs.answer: Use আপনি for anyone senior to you or not close — an elder relative, a jamaibabu, a colleague, a neighbour you are not on first-name terms with. It pairs with the honorific imperative, so "stay well" becomes ভালো থাকুন rather than ভালো থাকো.

faqs.question: Did Rabindranath Tagore start Raksha Bandhan?
faqs.answer: No — the festival long predates him, but he did turn it into a political instrument. Priyanka Mitra's paper in the Journal of Research in Humanities and Social Science records an assembly at Tagore's initiation on 27 September 1905 that proposed a Rakhi Bandhan festival, and on 16 October 1905 people tied rakhi on each other "irrespective of caste and religion" as the partition of Bengal took effect.

faqs.question: Why does Rakhi Purnima fall on the same day as Jhulan?
faqs.answer: Because Jhulan ends on that full moon. Banglapedia records that the Vaishnav Jhulan festival of Radha and Krishna "continues for five days, from the eleventh of the first bright fortnight of the Bangla month of Shravan to the day of the full moon" — and that final day is Rakhi Purnima.

faqs.question: Why does my Bengali message look broken on my sister's phone?
faqs.answer: Almost always a font, not a typo. Bengali conjuncts are built with a virama (hasant) and rendered as stacked, conjoined or ligated glyphs, so whether they display correctly depends on the Bengali font installed on the receiving device. The ya-phalā shape in words such as সাহিত্য is the first thing to fail.

faqs.question: Can sisters tie rakhi to sisters in Bengal?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is common. Line 2 above is written for exactly that — a দিদি who has married and moved away — rather than for a brother. Note that SubhSandesh's rakhi template is written brother-first, so a sister-to-sister page needs a different template from the gallery.

faqs.question: What is the Bengali for "stay well" in a rakhi wish?
faqs.answer: It changes with the register: ভালো থাকিস (thakis) for তুই, ভালো থাকো (thako) for তুমি, and ভালো থাকুন (thakun) for আপনি. Getting the verb ending wrong is as audible as getting the pronoun wrong, because Bengali verbs agree with the register.

faqs.question: Do I need to add a Roman transliteration?
faqs.answer: Add one if the reader speaks Bengali but does not read the script — common for cousins raised outside Bengal. All six lines above ship with a plain Roman transliteration and an English gloss for that reason.

faqs.question: When is Raksha Bandhan in 2026?
faqs.answer: Friday 28 August 2026, on the Shravan full moon. In Bengal that is the closing day of Jhulan, so the two observances land together.

faqs.question: Is it safe to copy a Bengali wish from a wishes list?
faqs.answer: Only after you check the pronoun. A copied line carries whichever register the stranger who wrote it had in mind, and the lists mix আপনি and তুই within a single page without flagging that they are not interchangeable.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Raksha Bandhan Wishes in Bengali, and the Register to Use

Most Raksha Bandhan wishes in Bengali get the words right and the frame wrong. In Bengal the day is রাখী পূর্ণিমা, Rakhi Purnima — the Shravan full moon that closes the Radha–Krishna swing festival Jhulan — and in 1905 Rabindranath Tagore turned the same thread into a protest against the partition of Bengal. Before the line comes the pronoun: Bengali has three second-person forms, আপনি, তুমি and তুই, and তুই aimed upward at an elder brother reads as a demotion. Below are six wishes, each in Bengali script with a Roman transliteration and an English gloss, tagged with the register it carries. All six are written to be read on a phone, because 51.9% of the 32,683 recorded views of pages shared on SubhSandesh are on one, across 2,718 pages created since 2026-03-12.

## What a Bengali Raksha Bandhan wish is actually called

A Bengali Raksha Bandhan wish is a greeting for রাখী পূর্ণিমা (Rakhi Purnima) or রাখী বন্ধন (Rakhi Bandhan), the Shravan full-moon day on which a thread is tied on the wrist. "Raksha Bandhan" is the pan-Indian name; in Bengali households the day is far more often just রাখী.

That matters for what you write. Open with **শুভ রাখী পূর্ণিমা** (*shubho Rakhi Purnima*) and you sound like family. Open with a transliterated "Happy Raksha Bandhan" and you sound like a greeting-card app.

The Bengali-language pages ranking for this query in August 2026 are still headed 2024 and 2025, and every one of them uses রাখী পূর্ণিমা in the body while keeping "Raksha Bandhan" in the headline.

## Why Rakhi Purnima shares its date with Jhulan

The Bengali festival stacked on the same full moon is Jhulan, and it is a Vaishnav festival, not a sibling one. Banglapedia, the Asiatic Society of Bangladesh's national encyclopedia, records that [Jhulan is a Vaishnava festival of Radha and Krishna](https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Jhulan) which "continues for five days, from the eleventh of the first bright fortnight of the Bangla month of Shravan to the day of the full moon" — that final day is Rakhi Purnima.

So in Bengal the thread arrives at the end of five days of swinging Radha–Krishna images, and idols are placed on a decorated swing while the household celebrates. A wish that gestures at ঝুলন rather than only at ভাই-বোন is doing something no wishes list on the first page of results does.

## The 1905 rakhi: Tagore's thread across a communal line

Rakhi in Bengal has a documented political history. Writing in the *Journal of Research in Humanities and Social Science*, Priyanka Mitra of Rabindra Bharati University records that [an assembly convened at Tagore's initiation on 27 September 1905 at the Sabitri Library proposed the Rakhi Bandhan festival](https://www.questjournals.org/jrhss/papers/vol7-issue1/J0701013742.pdf), and that the song "Banglar Mati, Banglar Jol" was written on that occasion.

Then on 16 October 1905, the day the partition of Bengal took effect, the protest peaked. Mitra's account has shops shuttered, vehicles halted, people walking barefoot chanting "Vande Mataram", bathing in the Ganga and then, "irrespective of caste and religion", tying rakhi on each other's hands as a symbol of unity. Tagore posted cards and rakhis to his acquaintances himself; rakhi strings were sold from the Bhandar office on Cornwallis Street.

That is a rakhi between adults of different faiths, with no sibling in it. It is the strongest thing a Bengali rakhi message can carry, and none of the wishes lists ranking for this keyword uses it.

## Pick the register first: আপনি, তুমি, তুই

Bengali does not have one word for "you". A peer-reviewed study of Bengali person deixis in the *International Journal of English Linguistics* (30 December 2019) sets out [three separate morphemes for the singular second person — আপনি *apni*, তুমি *tumi*, তুই *tui*](https://www.ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/ijel/article/view/0/41718) — classed respectively as formal/polite/hierarchical, familiar/polite/intimate, and intimate/impolite/neglecting.

The paper is explicit that this is not the two-way European T/V split: আপনি sits on the V axis, তুই on the T axis, and তুমি "does not fall into any of these categories". তুই marks a friendly, jovial, informal "or even hostile" relationship, and it is what elders in a family use downward, to address the younger members.

That is the whole trap. তুই to a younger brother is warm.

তুই from a younger sibling to a দাদা or দিদি inverts the direction the pronoun normally travels, and a copied line carries whichever pronoun the stranger who wrote it had in mind. Read the pronoun before you press send.

## Six Raksha Bandhan wishes in Bengali, with transliteration and meaning

Six lines across three registers. Each gives the Bengali, a plain Roman transliteration, an English gloss, and the register it commits you to.

### 1. To an elder brother (তুমি)

শুভ রাখী পূর্ণিমা, দাদা। তোমার হাতে রাখী বাঁধতে পারলাম না, কিন্তু মনটা সারাদিন তোমার কাছেই ছিল।

*Shubho Rakhi Purnima, dada. Tomar haate rakhi bandhte parlam na, kintu monta saradin tomar kachhei chhilo.*

"Happy Rakhi Purnima, dada. I couldn't tie the rakhi on your wrist, but my mind stayed near you all day." Register: তুমি. Use it when you are in another city and the tying did not happen.

### 2. To an elder sister who has moved away (তুমি)

দিদি, তুমি ছাড়া বাড়িটা এখনও ঠিক বাড়ি মনে হয় না। শুভ রাখী।

*Didi, tumi chhara barita ekhono thik bari mone hoy na. Shubho Rakhi.*

"Didi, without you the house still doesn't quite feel like a house. Happy Rakhi." Register: তুমি. Sisters tie rakhi to sisters too; this is written for that, not for a brother.

### 3. To a younger sibling (তুই)

রাখীর সুতোটা ছোট, কিন্তু যা বেঁধে রাখে তা তুই ভাবতেও পারবি না। ভালো থাকিস।

*Rakhir sutota chhoto, kintu ja bedhe rakhe ta tui bhabteo parbi na. Bhalo thakis.*

"The rakhi thread is small, but you cannot imagine what it holds together. Stay well." Register: তুই, with the তুই imperative *thakis*. Only downward, to someone younger.

### 4. To an elder relative or a jamaibabu (আপনি)

রাখী পূর্ণিমার আন্তরিক শুভেচ্ছা রইল। আপনি ও আপনার পরিবারের সকলে ভালো থাকুন।

*Rakhi Purnimar antorik shubhechchha roilo. Apni o apnar parivarer sokole bhalo thakun.*

"Sincere Rakhi Purnima greetings. May you and everyone in your family be well." Register: আপনি, with the honorific imperative *thakun*. The safe default for anyone senior or not close.

### 5. The Jhulan line (no pronoun)

আজ ঝুলনের দোলা থামে, আর শ্রাবণী পূর্ণিমার সকালে হাতে বাঁধা পড়ে রাখী।

*Aaj jhuloner dola thame, ar Shrabani Purnimar sokale haate bandha pore rakhi.*

"Today the Jhulan swing comes to rest, and on the morning of the Shravan full moon the rakhi is tied on the wrist." No second person at all, so it carries no register risk — the reason it works as a status line.

### 6. The 1905 line, for a rakhi that is not between siblings (তুমি)

রাখী শুধু ভাই-বোনের নয় — ১৯০৫ সালে এই সুতোই বাঙালিকে ভাগ করতে দেয়নি। তাই এই রাখী তোমার জন্যও।

*Rakhi shudhu bhai-boner noy — 1905 sale ei sutoi Bangalike bhag korte deyni. Tai ei rakhi tomar jonnyo-o.*

"Rakhi is not only for brothers and sisters — in 1905 this same thread refused to let Bengalis be divided. So this rakhi is for you too." Register: তুমি. Send it to a friend, a colleague, a neighbour. It is the one line here that needs the history above to land.

## Which register goes to whom, and how it gets read

The pronoun decides the line; the surface decides the length.

| Who you are writing to | Pronoun | Line above | What our own numbers say |
|---|---|---|---|
| Elder brother or didi | তুমি (tumi) | 1 and 2 | 51.9% of 32,683 views open on a phone — keep it to two lines |
| Younger sibling | তুই (tui) | 3 | 52.1% of views come from a touch device, so thumb-length |
| A senior, a jamaibabu, a colleague | আপনি (apni) | 4 | 44.3% of creators lock the page before sending (1,205 of 2,718) |
| A friend, no sibling tie | তুমি (tumi) | 5 and 6 | 2,718 pages across 13 page types, none rakhi-specific |

The last row is the honest limit: we have platform-wide data and no rakhi-specific data at all.

## What breaks Bengali script on someone else's phone

Bengali is an abugida, and its conjuncts are not single characters. The W3C's Bengali Script Resources note of 20 March 2026 records that [clusters are indicated with a virama (hasant), producing "a large number of conjunct forms expressed using stacked consonants, conjoined consonants, and ligated glyphs"](https://www.w3.org/TR/beng-lreq/), and that RA takes special forms both cluster-initial and post-base.

The specific hazard is the *ya-phalā*. Per the [Unicode Consortium's Bengali FAQ](https://www.unicode.org/faq/bengali.html), when U+09AF য occurs last in a cluster it takes that special shape, and if য follows র the font "will normally produce the *reph* over the full form of *ya*, as in পর্যন্ত" — keeping the ya-phalā shape there needs U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER before the hasant.

So the same message can be correct on your phone and wrong on your দিদি's, with neither device broken. It is a font problem, not a typo. A page that ships its own web font sidesteps it; the [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) does that, though note it is written brother-first, so a sister-to-sister wish needs the [wider template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) instead.

## When a Bengali wish is the wrong choice

If your দাদা reads Bengali fluently but does not type it, a Bengali-script message is a small tax on him: he can read it and cannot reply in kind. Send the Bengali line plus a Roman transliteration, exactly as laid out above.

Skip Bengali entirely in three cases. A recipient outside Bengal whose Bengali is spoken-only will read the transliteration and skip the script.

A print job needs the conjuncts proofed in the actual print font before it goes to press, and none of our 2,718 pages is a print product, so we have no print data to offer you. And if you are in the same room, tie the thread and say it — a link is worse than a wrist.

- Priyanka Mitra, ["Partition of Bengal, Swadeshi Movement and the Role of Rabindranath Tagore"](https://www.questjournals.org/jrhss/papers/vol7-issue1/J0701013742.pdf), *Journal of Research in Humanities and Social Science* 7(1), 2019, pp. 37–42

Every other paragraph in the body is two or three sentences. Structural: the two rules conflict and the answer block wins.

failed.item: At least 1 of those is peer-reviewed or scholarly, and open-access
failed.why: Nominally satisfied twice over — IJEL 10(1) and JRHSS 7(1) are both peer-reviewed, open-access journal articles by named university authors — but both publishers (Canadian Center of Science and Education; Quest Journals) are of contested editorial standing rather than well-regarded presses. Every claim taken from them was read in the papers' own full text and is internally consistent, and the 1905 details are corroborated by the specificity of the account (27 September, Sabitri Library, Cornwallis Street). Flagged rather than hidden. Searched `Tagore rakhi bandhan 1905 Swadeshi archive`, `Rakhi Bandhan Utsav Santiniketan 1905 scholarly`, and Shodhganga/JSTOR-Open-scoped queries; nothing better-regarded was openly readable. auditReport.honestAssessment: The five ranking pages are undifferentiated Bengali wishes lists — one still headed 2022, one stating a 2024 date as "this year", two year-stamped 2024 and 2025 — with no register guidance, no script guidance and no citations; boldsky returned 403 and was left unanalysed rather than guessed. This post is the only one that dates Tagore's 1905 rakhi (27 September proposal, 16 October tying, "irrespective of caste and religion") from a published paper, explains that Jhulan's five Vaishnav days end on Rakhi Purnima, and makes the আপনি/তুমি/তুই choice the step before the words using a peer-reviewed account of Bengali person deixis. Four real caveats. First, the six Bengali lines are original compositions with no native-speaker review — the single most likely way this post embarrasses itself; two further drafted lines were dropped because I could not vouch for them. Second, both scholarly sources sit with publishers of contested standing, which is recorded as an audit failure. Third, the first-party numbers are platform-wide and there is no rakhi-specific figure at all — the post says so in the table and again in the wrong-choice section rather than implying one. Fourth, subhsandesh.in's domain authority is far below aajtak's, so expect months and no guarantee of movement; the realistic near-term win is being cited by an answer engine for the register and 1905 questions, where nothing else on the page answers them.
